checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified the bird as a non-breeding male or female Brambling based on plumage (brownish-grey head/upperparts, orange breast). Consequently, it correctly marked 'Breeding male has a black head...' and 'Breeding male has bright orange-rufous... with black upperparts' as False. However, the Router was too lenient on the 'Flight displays distinctive white wing bars...' checkpoint. While white markings are visible, the specific diagnostic 'white outer tail feathers' are not clearly distinguishable in this static pose; the tail appears dark with only faint edging. Marking this as fully 'Present' is an overstatement of visual evidence. The bill color description ('yellowish-grey') aligns well with winter plumage. The leg anatomy check was marked present by the Router, but expert hints suggest verifying toe count; visually, the feet appear somewhat simplified/muddy, though not catastrophically wrong.
artifact_review: The Router reported no artifacts. However, visual inspection reveals subtle generation issues. 1) The feet/toes lack distinct definition; they appear slightly fused to the branch and to each other, lacking the crisp separation of individual toes expected in high-quality imagery. 2) The transition between the orange breast and white belly shows slight digital banding/smudging rather than a natural feather gradient. 3) The eye lacks a distinct catchlight, giving it a flat, 'dead' appearance common in AI generations. These are minor but present defects that lower the artifact score from perfect.
alignment_reasoning: Strong alignment with non-breeding/female Brambling taxonomy. Router correctly handled mutually exclusive breeding checkpoints. Deduction applied for over-claiming visibility of 'white outer tail feathers' which are not clearly resolved. Plumage colors and body shape are accurate.
artifact_reasoning: Router missed subtle structural/textural defects. Feet show mild fusion/lack of toe definition against the branch. Breast-to-belly color transition exhibits slight banding. Eye lacks realistic catchlight. These prevent a perfect artifact score but do not constitute catastrophic failure.

self_reflection_notes: Adjusted scores downward after self-reflection. This structural ambiguity warrants a stricter penalty than initially assigned. Checklist items #2 (Expert Evidence Utilization) and #4 (Leniency Bias) triggered these adjustments.
